impl.lines: 106-126 (create_process_timer_callback, the hardcoded signal at 111) and 129-147 (PosixTimerManager::new, the callback cloned into all three timers at 134-138)

root_cause: One shared callback closure carries a compile-time-constant signal number, and all three of the process's interval timers are built from clones of it. create_process_timer_callback (timer_manager.rs:106-126) takes only a Weak<Process> - there is no signal parameter - and its body constructs KernelSignal::new(SIGALRM) at line 111, with SIGALRM imported unconditionally at line 17. That closure is boxed into a single WorkItem at lines 117-118, and the returned outer closure (120-125) merely re-submits that same WorkItem on every expiry. PosixTimerManager::new then calls it once at line 132 and hands clones to all three timers: alarm_timer via RealTimeClock::timer_manager() at 134, virtual_timer over prof_clock.user_clock() at 136-137, and prof_timer over the full prof_clock at 138. Because WorkItem is cloned by handle rather than rebuilt, the three timers do not merely share the same code - they share the same work item, whose payload can only ever enqueue signal 14. So the timer selection in sys_setitimer (setitimer.rs:43-47) correctly routes ITIMER_VIRTUAL to virtual_timer and ITIMER_PROF to prof_timer, the clocks correctly diverge (virtual advances only in the user branch of update_cpu_time at timer_manager.rs:70-77, prof advances in both and is polled unconditionally at 78-81), the expiry fires, and then all three paths converge on the one closure and enqueue SIGALRM. The child's SIG_DFL disposition for signal 14 is SigDefaultAction::Term (sig_action.rs:163-164 catch-all), so it dies by SIGALRM and WTERMSIG reports 14. Nothing is missing from the surrounding machinery: SIGVTALRM = 26 and SIGPROF = 27 are already defined (signal/constants.rs:55-56), already ordered for delivery (sig_queues.rs:165), already print correctly (sig_num.rs:74-75), and already default to Term via the same catch-all - they are simply never constructed anywhere in kernel/src (grep finds only those definition/ordering/naming sites, zero senders).
invariant: A process interval timer must, on expiry, raise the signal that belongs to its own timer type: ITIMER_REAL raises SIGALRM, ITIMER_VIRTUAL raises SIGVTALRM, and ITIMER_PROF raises SIGPROF. The signal identity is a property of the individual timer, fixed when that timer is created, not a property shared by the process's timer set - so no two timers of different types may share an expiry action.
owning_layer: The process timer-management layer that constructs the timers - PosixTimerManager in kernel/src/process/process/timer_manager.rs, specifically the create_process_timer_callback factory it uses at line 132. That factory must take the signal number as a parameter so each of the three create_timer calls at lines 134-138 binds its own, because that is the only place in Asterinas where the timer-type-to-signal association can be established: by the time sys_setitimer has picked a timer (setitimer.rs:43-47) the callback is already baked in, and by the time the callback runs the timer core (time/core/timer.rs) has erased which timer it belongs to - process_expired_timers just calls callback.call() with no type information. Do NOT push the fix down into the timer core or up into the syscall entry: the core is generic over Fn(TimerGuard) and correctly knows nothing about signals, and the syscall entry only selects an already-built timer.
linux_reference: Linux keeps the signal number out of the timer and passes it in per call site, which is exactly the parameterization missing here. In kernel/time/posix-cpu-timers.c, check_process_timers() calls the shared helper check_cpu_itimer() twice with different signo arguments - check_cpu_itimer(tsk, &sig->it[CPUCLOCK_PROF], ..., SIGPROF) and check_cpu_itimer(tsk, &sig->it[CPUCLOCK_VIRT], ..., SIGVTALRM) - and the helper ends in send_signal_locked(signo, SEND_SIG_PRIV, tsk, PIDTYPE_TGID). So one body, one signal argument per timer type, delivered process-directed (PIDTYPE_TGID) rather than to a specific thread. ITIMER_REAL is a separate path entirely (an hrtimer whose it_real_fn sends SIGALRM, in kernel/time/itimer.c), not this file. Two details confirm Asterinas's surrounding design already matches: CPUCLOCK_VIRT samples utime only while CPUCLOCK_PROF samples utime+stime, mirroring virtual_timer over user_clock vs prof_timer over the full prof_clock; and PIDTYPE_TGID delivery matches Process::enqueue_signal (process/mod.rs:641), which is process-directed. Note the placement is the enforcement point, not merely the code: Linux never stores a signal in the timer state, so the two CPU itimers cannot alias each other the way Asterinas's cloned WorkItem does. Read via search results for posix-cpu-timers.c (codebrowser.dev cross-reference) and setitimer(2) on man7.org, since direct web fetches of elixir.bootlin.com and raw.githubusercontent.com are blocked from this container.
other_callers: create_process_timer_callback has exactly one caller in the whole tree (timer_manager.rs:132, verified by grep), so the blast radius of parameterizing it is confined to the three timers it builds. Of those, alarm_timer is the one with other consumers and it must keep SIGALRM: sys_alarm (syscall/alarm.rs:14) arms it, and procfs pid/task/stat.rs:201 reads its remaining time - both stay correct as long as SIGALRM is passed explicitly at line 134 rather than removed. virtual_timer and prof_timer are reached only by sys_setitimer/sys_getitimer (setitimer.rs:45-46, 92-93) plus the internal CPU-clock tick sites at timer_manager.rs:74 and 79, so no third-party caller depends on today's wrong signal. The separate create_prof_timer/create_virtual_timer methods (timer_manager.rs:165-178, and the PosixThread pair at posix_thread/mod.rs:280-288) take their own callback from the caller and are used only by timer_create (timer_create.rs:139-168), so POSIX timers are unaffected and this is not a shared-defect situation - the honest answer is that nobody outside setitimer sees the bug. This does mean the fix is genuinely narrow, but the layer choice still matters: fixing it anywhere below PosixTimerManager::new would require inventing timer-type knowledge in code that correctly has none.
suggested_direction: Give create_process_timer_callback a signal parameter and bind it per timer at construction. Change the signature at timer_manager.rs:106-108 to take a SigNum alongside the Weak<Process>, use it at line 111 in place of the hardcoded SIGALRM, and import SIGVTALRM and SIGPROF next to SIGALRM at line 17 (all three already exist in process/signal/constants.rs:55-56). Then drop the single `let callback = ...` at line 132 and call the factory once per timer at 134-138, passing SIGALRM for alarm_timer, SIGVTALRM for virtual_timer, and SIGPROF for prof_timer - the .clone() calls disappear with it, which is the point: three independent WorkItems instead of one aliased one. Purely additive and localized; no new subsystem, no change to the timer core, the syscall entry, or the signal layer. An alternative worth considering is reusing the existing enqueue_signal_async helper (process/mod.rs:816-828), which already takes a SigNum and submits a High-priority work item doing exactly the upgrade-and-enqueue this closure does by hand - that would let the callback become a one-liner, at the cost of allocating a work item per expiry instead of cloning a cached one, which matters because these timers re-arm on an interval and fire repeatedly. Verification note: SIGVTALRM and SIGPROF both fall through to SigDefaultAction::Term via the catch-all at sig_action.rs:163-164, so SIG_DFL termination already reports the right WTERMSIG once the correct signal is enqueued; no sig_action change is needed. Guard against regression at both ends - alarm01/alarm02 and ITIMER_REAL must still deliver SIGALRM, and setitimer02 (already enabled at all.txt:1437) must stay green.
